_comment: Why each shipped rule and file changed, read by install.py and never installed. Each list holds the versions the bundle has published, oldest first, as the sha256 of the rule body (rules) or of the file (files) with a one-line note saying why it differs from the version before it; only the first entry may have an empty note. A {"removed": true} entry ends a rule or file the bundle no longer ships. Notes are read by strangers: no task numbers, no commit hashes.

prompt-lessons-home.note: prompt-lessons.md is retired: its rules on writing briefs moved to writing-executor-briefs.md, which now covers prompts and briefs the user writes too.

executor-briefs-home.note: No longer lists "pinned expectations". That rule was removed from `writing-executor-briefs.md` because it rested on a single incident, and the routing rule says one case does not make a rule.
No longer sends test work to writing-executor-briefs.md: the rules on proving a test can fail moved to the proving-tests-can-fail skill, which loads itself when tests are added or changed.

Also covers writing any brief or prompt for an agent, including one the user asks for help with, and names its new section on what a brief must spell out; it takes over from the retired prompt-lessons.md.

lesson-routing.note: Adds one exception: a single case the user rules too costly to wait on goes into its home now, untagged, with the reason recorded in the ledger's origin log. The sentence explaining why "provisional" tags fail is gone; probes showed routing behaves the same without it.
Adds the proving-tests-can-fail skill as a fifth home for lessons, for the agent proving a test can fail. Its probes were re-run (B to F, three runs each) and all routed as expected.
Four homes instead of five: a lesson about writing a brief or prompt, by the agent or the user, goes to writing-executor-briefs.md now that prompt-lessons.md is retired.

search-silence.note: Shortened: sentences that only explained why the rule matters, not when it applies, were cut. A check for lost meaning found every instruction kept.

Narrowed to one job: before removing an established behaviour, find out whether it was ever designed, and don't treat a search that finds nothing as permission. The parts on choosing the kind of source, naming what was searched in a claim that something is absent, and same-kind sources agreeing were removed: real sessions on a current model already did all three without the rule. Its opening line changed, so a copy from before rules had IDs shows it as new beside the old rule's removal.

say-what-you-searched.note: New: when you report that something isn't there, say in the claim what you searched and how; a keyword search covers only its words. It restores, in plainer words, a part removed from the search-silence rule in the same release, after a real case on a current model showed it is still needed.

end-of-turn-text.note: Replaces the rule against opening a question panel after prose, whose reason was wrong. Text written before any tool call, not only a question panel, reaches the user as another model's short summary, which can change its meaning, so anything they must read goes in the text that ends the turn.
Drops the sentence naming the model the rule was checked on; that record belongs beside its probe in doc-test-probes.md, which has it.

self-carrying-sentences.note: Shortened: sentences that only explained why the rule matters, not when it applies, were cut. Agents given the old and the new wording acted the same in the same test scenarios.

Reworded so its opening says when it applies (what the agent tells the user, not docs it writes), with plain words in place of "coinage" and "minted". Agents given the old and the new wording acted the same in the same test scenarios.

observable-vs-inferred.note: Shortened: sentences that only explained why the rule matters, not when it applies, were cut. Agents given the old and the new wording acted the same in the same test scenarios.

The method for testing a rule's wording on a fresh agent moved to writing-standing-docs.md, where rule writing is covered; this rule keeps "test it instead" with an example that is not about docs. Agents acted the same in the same test scenarios.

Reworded in plainer words, and narrowed to its first part: explaining your own behaviour. The parts on explaining how a system or its data works and on picking numbers were removed: real sessions on a current model already did both without the rule. Its opening line changed, so a copy from before rules had IDs shows it as new beside the old rule's removal.

rule-into-code.note: The opening now says when the rule applies: when a fix depends on someone remembering to apply it, check whether code can make the correction instead. Same rule otherwise, in plainer words.

second-real-example.note: Shortened: sentences that only explained why the rule matters, not when it applies, were cut. Agents given the old and the new wording acted the same in the same test scenarios. One clause stayed because the test showed it was needed: an amendment does not inherit the maturity of the rule it extends.
Capitals used for emphasis are lowercased; nothing else changed.

existence-vs-magnitude.note: Shortened: sentences that only explained why the rule matters, not when it applies, were cut. A check for lost meaning found every instruction kept.
Capitals used for emphasis are lowercased; nothing else changed.

broken-instrument.note: Removed: it rested on a single incident, and the routing rule says one case does not make a rule.

measure-reach.note: Added: a fix scoped to the one example a report names can leave the same cause in place elsewhere, so the rule has the agent check how far the cause reaches first.

prompt-lessons.md.note: Points at the new end-of-turn-text rule in place of the old question-panel rule.
Retired: its rules on writing briefs moved to writing-executor-briefs.md, and each rule's cases go in the origin logs of lesson-candidates.md.

writing-standing-docs.md.note: Rules based on a single incident removed, as the routing rule requires.

The cold-test rule gains the method moved from the user-level rules file: have a fresh agent act on a wording, never ask it whether the wording is clear. A new closing section lists what a new or reworded rule must pass before it is proposed: its opening names the situation, Claude wouldn't do it unprompted (checked by running a session without it), it does one job in the right place, nothing in it goes out of date, it contradicts no other rule, and its wording is calm and concrete. The cold-test rule now opens with when it applies (when you test a rule) and drops capitals used for emphasis. The checklist's line on calm wording now follows Anthropic's guidance: write a rule as a plain instruction, not a forceful one, and leave out catch-alls like "if in doubt, do X"; keep emphasis (capitals, IMPORTANT) for one rule that sessions show being skipped, on that line alone; put a rule that must hold every time in a hook.
Points to the origin logs in lesson-candidates.md for each rule's cases, now that prompt-lessons.md is retired.

writing-executor-briefs.md.note: Rules based on a single incident removed, as the routing rule requires. Three stay even so, because an executor uses them at every checkpoint, where a repeat would cost too much to wait for a second case. All three are about showing that a new test really catches the bug it was written for, rather than passing whatever the code does: if the fix changed how a function is called, undoing it makes the test crash rather than fail, which proves nothing, so put the old behaviour back behind the new call instead; undo only the change being tested, not the whole file, so a failure has one possible cause; and when the test covers code that already worked, so there is no fix to undo, break the code deliberately and check the test fails.

The rules on proving a test can fail moved to the new proving-tests-can-fail skill, split into seven rules that each open on when they apply; this file keeps a pointer for briefing a sub-agent that writes tests. The rule on sizing delegated checkpoints is split into four, each opening on when it applies, and no longer says sub-agents are cut off routinely or without a report, since Claude Code now tells Claude when a run is cut off. The caller-audit rule is split into three: report every caller, verify a proposed fix separately from its findings, and also find code that depends on what a changed symbol's answers mean. Capitals used for emphasis are also lowercased.

New section on what a brief must spell out, moved from the retired prompt-lessons.md: the doc-editing rules a cold agent needs, computable corrections specified as code, a second real case before a lesson is recorded, and how findings are presented. The file now also covers prompts the user asks for help with.

doc-test-probes.md.note: Adds probes for the routing rule's new exception (one checks it works when the user rules a case too costly to wait on, one checks it stays the user's call), and a probe showing whether text written before a tool call still reaches the user only as a summary, with the model and version it was last checked on.
The routing probes carry the rule's new fifth home, and a new Probe F checks that a testing lesson with two contrasting cases routes to the proving-tests-can-fail skill.
The routing probes carry the rule's four homes: a lesson about writing a brief or prompt goes to writing-executor-briefs.

skills/finalise/scripts/context_budget_r.note: Also lists bookkeeping in the files loaded every session: dated notes in brackets, "Provisional" and "cold-tested" tags, and a CLAUDE.md longer than the 200 lines Claude Code's documentation recommends. A dated note on a standing permission is not listed.

skills/finalise/SKILL.md.note: Answers to `/finalize` as well as `/finalise`. Pushes without asking only where a `CLAUDE.md` explicitly pre-authorizes routine pushes; otherwise it still asks.
Step 5 asks for a response to each item the budget report lists as bookkeeping: move it out of the always-loaded file, or say why it stays.

Step 2 also points at the list in writing-standing-docs.md that a new or reworded rule must pass before it is proposed. Corrected two pointers: the user-level rule on plain wording lets the user's own terms stand (it never exempted project jargon), and the replace-not-join rule lives in writing-standing-docs.md. Adds the proving-tests-can-fail skill as a fifth home for lessons (step 1 now counts five), for the agent proving a test can fail. The routing test and the list of files it commits name it. "What NOT to record" no longer repeats the routing tests; it points to step 1's, which also corrects its old claim that every lesson that doesn't transfer goes to memory or decisions.md. Step 1 now captures a lesson candidate only for a mistake that cost or nearly cost something: the user catching something wrong by a standard already in force (not a new preference, which is feedback), several attempts or turns, or a wrong result reaching or about to reach a file, plan, report or the user. A better approach with no failure behind it is recorded as a decision, except a sharper way to write a prompt or brief, which may still be suggested as a prompt lesson. Capitals used for emphasis are also lowercased.

Four user-scope homes instead of five now that prompt-lessons.md is retired; the bullet is renamed "Lesson opportunities" and no longer offers a sharper way to write a prompt as a lesson with no failure behind it, which is a decision. The cross-check reads the candidate's own home.

skills/bootstrap-project/SKILL.md.note: Capitals used for emphasis are lowercased; nothing else changed.

skills/next/SKILL.md.note: No longer names the test rules among what writing-executor-briefs.md holds; they moved to the proving-tests-can-fail skill. Capitals used for emphasis are also lowercased.
The summary gives each task's backlog number every time it mentions one, and says so when an item has none.

commands/memory-audit.md.note: Part 1 adds a rule-by-rule pass over both CLAUDE.md files: where each rule should load, which sentences are only reasons or bookkeeping and can go, and a check of each trim before it is proposed.

The rule-by-rule pass checks each rule against the list in writing-standing-docs.md instead of its own, and no longer tells the reviewer to cut the short reasons that say what a rule protects. The actor test is cited as /finalise step 1 (it said step 2), the checklist's last step is called the cold test as that file calls it, and a line about /memory that no longer matched Claude Code was cut. Adds the proving-tests-can-fail skill as a fifth home for lessons, for the agent proving a test can fail. The audit's list of rule homes includes it. Capitals used for emphasis are also lowercased.
The list of rule homes drops the retired prompt-lessons.md; writing-executor-briefs.md now covers briefs and prompts the user writes too.

lesson-candidates.md.note: The ledger template gains a field recording a severity ruling, for a rule promoted on one case.

Names the rule the harness tests by its ID, self-carrying-sentences, not "the clarity rule". The candidate template's "Would live in" list includes the proving-tests-can-fail skill. Each case now records the model and Claude Code version it happened on, so a later review can tell which rules to re-check after a model change. The capture section says what counts as a case: a mistake that cost or nearly cost something. Capitals used for emphasis are also lowercased.
The "Would live in" field no longer offers the retired prompt-lessons.md, and the capture section names /finalise's renamed "Lesson opportunities" bullet.

under-explained-cases.md.note: Names the rule this log serves by its ID and current wording; it quoted the rule's old opening.

rules/standing-docs.md.note: New: loads a pointer to writing-standing-docs.md whenever Claude reads or edits a CLAUDE.md, skill, memory or other instruction file in the session's project, so the doc-editing rules are read without relying on the CLAUDE.md pointer alone.

rules/tests.md.note: Loads when Claude opens a test file and tells it to load the proving-tests-can-fail skill.

skills/proving-tests-can-fail/SKILL.md.note: New skill: the rules on proving a test can fail before trusting it (write the test first, revert only the fix, break working code on purpose to check new tests). Claude loads it when adding or changing tests; in tests it loaded every time, including when the request never mentioned tests. Capitals used for emphasis are also lowercased.
